fact: 1921年英国爆发大规模失业危机。失业率从年初的6%升至3月底的11%；6月底（不含煤矿业）受保工人失业率达19%、工会会员失业率达23%，为该部门有记录以来最高。12月30日就业交易所登记失业人数达188.6万（男145.1万、女33.4万），而1920年底仅为75.7万。6月时就业交易所向300多万完全或部分失业工人支付救济金，另有100多万不合格领取救济的矿工闲置。

sources.title: Ministry of Labour Gazette, January 1922（英国劳工部月报）
sources.quote: The proportion unemployed rose from 6 per cent. at the beginning of the year to 11 per cent. at the end of March... At the end of June the proportion of unemployed, apart from the coal mining industry, had risen to 19 per cent. among insured workpeople and to 23 per cent. among members of those Trade Unions making returns. These figures are the highest ever recorded by the Department. ... The total number on the Live Registers of the Employment Exchanges at 30th December, 1921, was 1,886,000.

sources.title: National Archives, Memorandum from the Minister of Labour on unemployment, 1921（CAB 24/127）
sources.quote: During June, the Employment Exchanges were paying Benefit to over three millions of wholly or partially unemployed workers and in addition over a million miners, ineligible for Benefit, were idle. ... in June not more than one out of every two industrial workers in the country, for a working population of over 12 millions, was engaged in whole-time employment.

fact: 1921年4月1日至7月4日，英国煤矿工人全国大罢工（lockout）持续约11周。起因是政府宣布3月31日恢复煤矿私有化，矿主宣布大幅削减工资和地区协议。矿工工会呼吁「三方同盟」（Triple Alliance）支持，但铁路工会领袖在4月15日「黑色星期五」撤回罢工通知。矿工被迫接受削减10%—40%工资的地区协议。此轮工资削减随后波及约600万工人。

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, Miners' and General Strikes
sources.quote: In February, the government announced that private control of the mines would resume on March 31. The mine owners announced drastic wage cuts and district agreements. The MFGB's refusal to accept these conditions led to the publication of lock-out notices... The miners fought on for 11 weeks until they were forced to accept district settlements and wage cuts that ranged between 10 and 40 percent. ... the defeat of the miners heralded a sweeping round of wage reductions that affected some 6 million workers.

sources.title: Ministry of Labour Gazette, May 1921
sources.quote: Of the total of 98 disputes in progress at some time during the month, by far the most important was that involving almost all the workpeople in the coal-mining industry, which began on 1st April and continued throughout the month. ... The total number of workpeople involved in all disputes in progress in April was nearly 1,200,000.

fact: 1921年3月《失业保险法》（Unemployment Insurance Act 1921）获御准，是应对大规模失业的核心立法。该法提供16周救济（3月至10月底），7月1日法案追加6周。但救济金从每周20先令降至15先令。该法还暂停了行业的「contract out」权利（即行业可选择退出保险基金），1927年才废除。1920年法案将几乎所有英国工人纳入保障（约1100万人），失业救济金为男性每周15先令、女性12先令。

sources.title: National Archives, Memorandum from the Minister of Labour on unemployment, 1921（CAB 24/127）
sources.quote: the finance of the Unemployment Insurance Act of last March is based upon the assumption that the numbers of unemployed person qualified for benefit will average 1,250,000 week by week throughout the period July 1921 to June 1922. ... the 16 weeks benefit to run from last March to the end of October (provided by the Act of last March) plus the additional 6 weeks of the Act of July 1st, is being exhausted week by week for increasingly large numbers of persons.

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Great Britain Establishes Unemployment Benefits
sources.quote: Under the act passed in 1920, weekly benefits were fixed at fifteen shillings for a man and twelve shillings for a woman, with half rates for young people. The Unemployed Workers' Dependents Act gave a married man eligible for benefits five shillings for his wife and one shilling for each dependent child under age fourteen. ... In 1921, for example, the power to 'contract out,' whereby an industry could exempt itself from contributing to the insurance fund, was suspended.

fact: 1921年4月煤矿罢工使煤炭严重短缺，用煤工业大面积瘫痪：生铁、锡板和陶瓷制造业几乎完全停产。英国煤炭出口价格下跌50%，政府每月花500万英镑补贴煤炭产业。德国煤炭作为凡尔赛赔款的一部分涌入世界市场，英国煤矿组织低效、技术落后，无法竞争。

sources.title: Ministry of Labour Gazette, May 1921
sources.quote: The depression in employment... was rendered much more acute, during April, by the increasing shortage of fuel resulting from the general stoppage of work at the coal mines. In most of the great coal-using industries employment was greatly reduced, and in some cases, e.g., pig-iron, tinplate, and pottery manufacture, it was almost at a standstill.

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, Miners' and General Strikes
sources.quote: The coal industry was particularly hard-hit by the slump in demand and by the flood of German coal that reached the world market as part of the Versailles reparations settlement. Britain's mines, hampered by inefficient organization and old-fashioned techniques, were unable to compete. The export price of British coal fell by 50 percent; by 1921 the government was spending 5 million a month to subsidize the industry.

fact: 1921年英国生活成本指数大幅下降：生活成本指数（含全部项目）在1921年下降12.8%（1922年再降17.5%），主要因进口价格下降。但名义工资率在1921年下降22.2%，实际工资（相对物价）反而略有上升。1920年4月至1921年1月间工资率上涨17%而物价下跌25%——工资滞后于物价变动。批发价格从1920年峰值下跌50%—60%。

sources.title: A.W. Phillips (1958), 引自Irving Fisher's Debt-Deflation Theory（学术论文）
sources.quote: in the United Kingdom unemployment rose from 2.6 percent in 1920 to 17.0 percent in 1921 and 14.3 percent in 1922, while wage rates declined by 22.2 percent in 1921 and 19.1 percent in 1922, and the cost of living index fell by 12.8 percent in 1921 — largely a result of falling import prices — and 17.5 percent in 1922.

sources.title: Oxford Pamphlets on Home Affairs No. H.3, The Transition from War to Peace
sources.quote: between April 1920 and January 1921 they [money wage-rates] had actually increased by 17 per cent. in the face of a price fall of 25 per cent.; and, while during the course of 1921 itself they fell again absolutely (by some 20 per cent.), relatively to prices they were still rising slightly.

fact: 1921年失业救济金为男性每周15先令、女性12先令（青年半额），已婚男子另有妻子5先令、每名14岁以下子女1先令的家属津贴。有分析认为失业男子及其家庭在此时期的境况可能优于有工作的非技术工人。国家保险计划为1900万工人及家属提供医疗保障。但救济金从20先令降至15先令，工会基金和私人储蓄大量消耗。

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Great Britain Establishes Unemployment Benefits
sources.quote: Under the act passed in 1920, weekly benefits were fixed at fifteen shillings for a man and twelve shillings for a woman, with half rates for young people. The Unemployed Workers' Dependents Act gave a married man eligible for benefits five shillings for his wife and one shilling for each dependent child under age fourteen... At least one analyst has suggested that an unemployed man and his family possibly were better off during this period than an unskilled laborer with a job.

sources.title: National Archives, CAB 24/127
sources.quote: Trade Union funds and private resources are to a large extent exhausted, the amount of the Benefit itself has been reduced from 20/- to 15/-.

fact: 1921年英国在金本位旧平价政策驱动下实施严厉通缩。英镑对美元从1920年初的3.18美元低点（比战前平价4.86低35%）回升到1922年初的约4.20美元。英格兰银行贴现率从1919年11月的5%升至1920年4月的7%，维持近一年。1921年4月起货币政策逐步放松，到1922年中降至3%。1918—1920年间政府开支削减75%。

sources.title: Bank of England Staff Working Paper No. 968, Turning in the widening gyre
sources.quote: Further efforts at fiscal consolidation were put on hold, though the large primary surplus achieved by 1920 was maintained and Bank Rate was kept at 7%. ... monetary policy, which was eased steadily from April 1921 to a trough of 3% in mid-1922. ... the sterling rose steadily from mid-1921 to reach 97% of parity by early 1923.

sources.title: The Postwar International Money Crisis（学术著作预览）
sources.quote: Its prewar parity had been $4.86, but by early 1920 it had dropped to a low $3.18, 35 per cent below par. Intent on restoring prewar parity and strengthening the currency, the British authorities responded by implementing severe deflationary policies in 1920/21. This led to a sharp drop in wages and prices (the latter falling by as much as 50-60 per cent from their peak levels in 1920).

fact: 1921年《失业保险法》暂停了行业的「contract out」权利（即行业可选择退出保险基金），将几乎所有工人强制纳入失业保险体系。1920年《失业保险法》覆盖约1100万工人。失业工人家属津贴（Unemployed Workers' Dependents Act）为已婚男子提供妻子5先令、每名子女1先令的补贴。济贫法（Poor Law）仍是最后一道安全网，但济贫委员10个月来支出巨大、难以持续。

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Great Britain Establishes Unemployment Benefits
sources.quote: In 1921, for example, the power to 'contract out,' whereby an industry could exempt itself from contributing to the insurance fund, was suspended; it was abolished in 1927. Aid to dependents of unemployed workers was added to relieve the suffering of families.

sources.title: National Archives, CAB 24/127
sources.quote: the expenditures of the Poor Law Guardians during the past 10 months have made it increasingly difficult for them to continue the relief which they have been giving either in supplement of Unemployment Benefit or to those not receiving it.

fact: 1921年英国传统工业（煤炭、钢铁、棉花、铁）面临全球供给过剩和价格下跌的困境。英国煤矿组织低效、技术落后，煤炭出口价格下跌50%。凡尔赛赔款安排使德国煤炭涌入世界市场。英国产业向化工、人造丝和汽车等新产业的转型缓慢。4月煤矿罢工使重工业几乎瘫痪，暴露了英国经济对煤炭的过度依赖。

sources.title: Economics Help, UK Economy in the 1920s
sources.quote: British industries, which had performed well in the nineteenth century, such as cotton, steel, coal and iron faced difficulties from global oversupply and falling prices. There was a sluggishness in switching resources from these old industries to new growth industries like chemicals, rayon and motor cars.

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, Miners' and General Strikes
sources.quote: Britain's mines, hampered by inefficient organization and old-fashioned techniques, were unable to compete. The export price of British coal fell by 50 percent.

fact: 1921年4月工资变动统计：超过114.7万工人遭受工资下调，每周工资总额减少超过27万英镑；仅1.8万人获得加薪（每周仅增约2700英镑）。煤炭、钢铁、造船等重工业失业率极高（煤炭业23%、造船和钢铁业36%）。农业和建筑业就业相对稳定。就业交易所登记的空缺岗位在4月底仅3.4万个（3月底4.1万个）。

sources.title: Ministry of Labour Gazette, May 1921
sources.quote: changes in rates of wages reported to the Department as having been arranged to come into operation in April affected over 1,165,000 workpeople, of whom about 1,147,000 sustained decreases, amounting to over £270,000 in their weekly wages, and over 18,000 received increases, amounting to about £2,700 a week.

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Great Britain Establishes Unemployment Benefits
sources.quote: The coal mining industry, after the strike of 1921, suffered from 23 percent unemployment, and 36 percent of the workers in shipbuilding and steel, industries that relied heavily on coal, were jobless.
